item.title: Judge orders refunds after Supreme Court strikes down Trump’s tariffs
item.description: A judge with the U.S. Court of International Trade has ordered refunds for companies that paid tariffs that were later struck down by the United States Supreme Court. America’s top court struck down U.S. President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” and fentanyl-related tariffs last month. item.title: Solomon tells OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that Tumbler Ridge deserves apology
item.description: Federal Artificial Intelligence Minister Evan Solomon says he met with the CEO of OpenAI and told him the people of Tumbler Ridge, B.C., deserve an apology for the tech firm's role in events leading up to the mass shooting there last month.

item.title: Maya, 12-year-old Tumbler Ridge shooting victim, showing small signs of improvement: parents
item.description: The parents of twelve-year-old Maya Gebala, who was shot in the head and neck during the mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, say that their daughter is showing small but steady signs of improvement.

item.title: New B.C. legislation cracks down on weapons, violence in supportive housing
item.description: The B.C. government has tabled legislation, which the housing minster says will make it easier to kick "problematic" tenants out of supportive housing.

item.title: TransLink clarifies plans for FIFA World Cup in Vancouver after questions over station closures
item.description: TransLink is clearing the air after some confusion over whether some SkyTrain stations would close during FIFA World Cup match days in Vancouver.

item.title: Canadian tourists revisiting Vegas trips with some casinos accepting CAD at par
item.description: More Canadians have been travelling to Las Vegas after some casinos in the desert city announced a currency parity program between the Canadian dollar and the U.S. dollar.

item.title: Province to tighten crane licensing after seven deaths in five years
item.description: The B.C. government announced a new crane licensing and permitting program on Tuesday after seven people had died in the province within the last five years.

item.title: New Westminster police arrest two, seize drugs and weapons from RV
item.description: New Westminster police have arrested two people and seized cash, weapons, and illicit drugs from inside an RV in the Clute Street area.

item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada can not yet rule out military participation in the escalating conflict in the Middle East. item.title: Mayor Sim expands apologies amid Orr misinformation controversy
item.description: Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim is still mired in the scandal over his false accusations that fellow council member Sean Orr had distributed drugs.
